title: Etale coverings refine to opens of finite locally free covers locally on the base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\{e_a:E_a\to S\}_{a\in A}$ be a small jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There exist a small Zariski open covering $S=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], surjective finite locally free morphisms $q_j:W_j\to U_j$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-finite-locally-free], and small Zariski open coverings $W_j=\bigcup_{k\in K_j}W_{j,k}$, such that for every $j,k$ there are $a(j,k)\in A$ and a morphism $h_{j,k}:W_{j,k}\to E_{a(j,k)}$ with $e_{a(j,k)}\circ h_{j,k}=u_j\circ q_j\circ\iota_{j,k}$, where $u_j:U_j\hookrightarrow S$ and $\iota_{j,k}:W_{j,k}\hookrightarrow W_j$ are the open inclusions. Empty schemes and empty indexing families are allowed.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take $J=\varnothing$. All required families and equations are then empty. Conversely, a jointly surjective empty family forces $S=\varnothing$. Hence assume $S$ nonempty. It suffices to produce, for each point $s\in S$, a suitable open neighbourhood $U_s$, since these neighbourhoods then cover $S$.

source.place: Tag 02LI, remark-topologies; empty case and pointwise reduction

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$. Joint surjectivity supplies $a\in A$ and $x\in E_a$ mapping to $s$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ containing $s$, and an affine open $E=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\subset e_a^{-1}(V)$ containing $x$, by the affine-open basis lemma. Restricting an etale morphism to open charts preserves its defining affine-local etale condition. Thus $E\to V$ is etale. Apply the existing locally-standard etale algebra lemma at the prime of $x$: there is $b\in B_0$ not in that prime and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $(B_0)_b\cong (R[t]/(f))_{\bar g}$, with $f$ monic and $f'$ invertible. The basic-open affine section lemma identifies $E^0=D_E(b)$ with this standard etale spectrum, over $V$, and $x\in E^0$. Denote the prime of $x$ in this algebra by $\mathfrak q$; it lies over the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $s$.

source.place: Tag 02LG, lemma-dominate-etale-neighbourhood-finite-flat, first proof paragraph; Algebra 00UE and Schemes 01IT, 01I3

proof.text: Apply the standard-etale prime-lift lemma to the algebra of $E^0$. It gives a finite free $R$-algebra $C$ and a surjection $\pi:T=\operatorname{Spec}C\to V$. Since $s\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, the ring $R$ is nonzero, so the free rank is positive; the finite-free spectrum lemma makes $\pi$ finite locally free. For every $t\in\pi^{-1}(s)$ its prime $\mathfrak q'$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$. The prime-lift lemma, with the fixed prime $\mathfrak q$ of $x$, supplies $c_t\notin\mathfrak q'$ and a map $B\to C_{c_t}$ taking that prime back to $\mathfrak q$. By the basic-open affine section lemma and contravariant functoriality of spectrum, this is a morphism $h_t:D_T(c_t)\to E^0\hookrightarrow E_a$ over $S$, with $h_t(t)=x$. In particular the opens $D_T(c_t)$ cover the entire fibre over $s$.

source.place: Tag 02LG, lemma-dominate-etale-neighbourhood-finite-flat, final proof sentence invoking Algebra 00UF

proof.text: Put $O=\bigcup_{t\in\pi^{-1}(s)}D_T(c_t)$ and $Z=T\setminus O$. Since $\pi$ is finite, the existing finite-closed-map lemma makes $\pi(Z)$ closed in $V$. No point of $Z$ lies over $s$, so $s\notin\pi(Z)$. By the principal-open basis lemma choose $\ell\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $U_s=D_V(\ell)\subset V\setminus\pi(Z)$. Therefore $\pi^{-1}(U_s)\subset O$. Set $W_s=\pi^{-1}(U_s)$ and $W_{s,t}=W_s\cap D_T(c_t)$. These are actual open subschemes and they cover $W_s$; the maps $h_t$ restrict along their open inclusions to maps $W_{s,t}\to E_a$.

source.place: Tag 02LI, remark-topologies, passage from 02LG fibre neighbourhoods to a covering after Zariski shrinking

proof.text: The restricted map $q_s:W_s\to U_s$ is still finite locally free, as follows explicitly in coordinates. The basic-open affine section lemma identifies $U_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R_\ell$ and $W_s=D_T(\ell)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_\ell$, using the image of $\ell$ in $C$. The localization-tensor isomorphism identifies the underlying $R_\ell$-module $C_\ell$ with $C\otimes_R R_\ell$. The free-module base-change lemma gives the finite basis $e_i\otimes1$, for the same $r$ indices as the $R$-basis of $C$. Hence the finite-free spectrum lemma applies to $R_\ell\to C_\ell$. Surjectivity needs no new theorem: any point of $U_s$ has a preimage under $\pi$, and that preimage is in $W_s$ by its definition. For each $t$, the equality over $S$ from Step 3 restricts to $e_a\circ h_{s,t}=u_s\circ q_s\circ\iota_{s,t}$.

source.place: Tag 02LI, remark-topologies; localization of the finite free algebra of 00UF (Algebra 00DK, Morphisms 02KB)

proof.text: Perform these choices for each $s\in S$, take $J$ to be the underlying point set of $S$, and put $K_s=\pi_s^{-1}(s)$. Each $s$ belongs to $U_s$, so the $U_s$ cover $S$. The finite-fibre lemma makes $K_s$ finite; Steps 4 and 5 give the required open covering of $W_s$, all maps, and the exact factorization equations. Put $a(s,t)=a_s$. The given schemes have small point sets and their rings and localizations stay within the universes of the size convention; these choices indexed by a small point set give a small Zariski covering, and each finite $K_s$ is small. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, Noetherian assumption, or finite-subcover choice on $S$ is used.
